newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods--U.S. Gulf firms on NYMEX strength.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods--U.S. Gulf firms on NYMEX strength.

text.p: U.S. Gulf gasoline differentials found the fuel to rise in the sharp gains made on NYMEX on Wednesday along with a tightening of supply of cash products, players said.

Differentials in New York Harbor reformulated gasoline also firmed slightly amid news of the shutdown of Tosco's Bayway catalytic cracking unit, while Midcontinent gasoline markets firmed, at least for August barrels.

On the NYMEX, August gasoline surged to settle up 3.43 cents at 69.90 cents a gallon -- the highest spot contract settlement since January. August heat, caught in the updraft, was up by 1.47 cents to 55.78 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF
Gulf gasoline differentials firmed slightly in moderate afternoon trade as supply remained tight and MTBE prices high.

Prompt back 22nd cycle "M1" grade conventional unleaded gasoline firmed about a quarter cent to 1.25/1.50 cents over the screen. Deals were done at 1.15 cents this morning and 1.60 cents this afternoon.
"Gasoline was the focus today," said a cash trader, noting August NYMEX gasoline's close at 69.90 cents a gallon.
Any month barrels for M1, which reaches a scheduling deadline on Friday, held steady at 3.00/2.75 cents under the print.
Riding a continuing strong price wave for MTBE, A1-grade reformulated gasoline held at a lofty 3.00/3.50 cents over the screen.
V1 93-octane premium grade gasoline differentials firmed about a half cent to 6.75/7.00 cents a gallon.
"There is hardly any supply," said a U.S. Gulf player.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Conventional M2 gasoline differentials ended near steady with the previous day's levels, traders said, though barrels for early August delivery weakened modestly to about 3.00 cents under the August futures, a dip of about 0.40 cent on the day.
Very prompt M2 gasoline differentials were talked near 2.00 cents under the NYMEX.
"It's all a function of timing, so it's a little hard to peg," one Harbor player said.
Reformulated A2 gasoline found some strength as the day wore on, with traders reporting a deal for prompt barrels done at 3.50 cents over the August futures, a gain of about 0.25 cent.
Players attributed much of the strength to the shutdown of Tosco Bayway's catalytic cracking unit Wednesday, though rumors had circulated earlier in the week that unit be shut.
MIDCONTINENT

A relatively low 18-day supply of gasoline inventories in the Williams Pipeline had the market in the Midcontinent talking, although activity was a bit subdued, particularly with the end of the month that had Group Three traders mostly interested in closing their books on July.

In the Group, the illiquid prompt July market for unleaded actually weakened, while the August market firmed amid unconfirmed reports early August barrels traded at 3.10 over September NYMEX on a relatively distressed basis.
Despite the near-term strength seen in the midcontinent, traders stressed that it was based on a homegrown version of the solid demand nationwide.
In the Chicago market, regular unleaded differentials for prompt material blew out by nearly 2.00 cents with deals heard done as high as 4.75 cents over the September print.
"Everyone's jumping on the bandwagon," said one trader, noting an industry outing last week in Cleveland left some players out of the action and with some catching up to do.
Also, second cycle and conventional unleaded barrels traded at 4.25 and 2.75 cents over September respectively.
